correctness.rationale: The narrowed claim is the exact leading Lipschitz deficit along the two prescribed one-leaf paths. Strict monotonicity in each datum and translation equivariance trap the new center s in (0,t); linear interpolation on unit arms gives numerator max(s,t−s) and boundary denominator t/2. Above 2 the center solves (1+s)^(p−1)−(1−s)^(p−1)+(m−3)s^(p−1)=(t−s)^(p−1). The first difference is 2(p−1)s+o(s), giving s=O(t^(p−1))=o(t) and then the nonzero coefficient 1/[2(p−1)]. Below 2 the balance is (m−2)s^(p−1)=(1−s)^(p−1)−(1+s−t)^(p−1); a uniform bound on the regular derivative first gives s=O(t^(1/(p−1)))=o(t), then the mean-value theorem makes the right side asymptotic to (p−1)t. The deficit is exactly 2s/t for small t on each path, producing the repaired exponents and coefficients. These estimates are for fixed m,p and do not extrapolate uniformly to p=2. The frozen finite bisection script was read, not executed or used to prove an asymptotic. The retained baseline comparison, two-leaf midpoint and Hilbert equality example also check out.
